And given the overlap between CDPR’s games with their elaborate open worlds and those of GTA 6, investors wanted to know how the latter’sÂ phenomenal success will impact the studio’s work.

Polish studio CD Projekt Red is known for its work on open-world adventures like The Witcher and Cyberpunk, and during the briefing investorsÂ asked whether the success of GTA will impact the design process and development of those series. CDPR explained that as much as the game is an “inspiration” to them, there is no need to adjust the development road maps for its upcoming games in response to the success of Rockstarâs work.

“We have certain ambitions when it comes to The Witcher and Cyberpunk 2, but they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6,” was the response given to an investor. “It’s always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done. That’s for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers.â That being said, if there were to be a comparison between the works of the two studios, CD Projekt Red believes that the long development time between The Witcher 3 and 4 has led to a comparable leap in fidelity for the company’s fantasy role-playing series to that seen between GTA 5 and 6.

Excluding the recent release of The Witcher 3 Remastered on modern consoles in September, CDPR’s last major video game release was 2020’s Cyberpunk 2077. Yet despite not having put out a new game in six years, revenue for the company has only grown, and anticipation for its work remains high. The release of The Witcher 3 Remastered saw the game record its highest concurrent player count in its history, with 138,000 players at once, despite the core game being over a decade old.

This is something the company credits to its work bringing in new players via broad multimedia expansion. The Witcher has received numerous TV series with Netflix, while the Cyberpunk: Edgerunners anime made in collaboration with Studio Trigger recently premiered its second season. CDPR noted that the show reached the top 10 in 55 countries on its release and debuted third on the streaming serviceâs global top 10. More importantly for the studio, it brought people back to playing Cyberpunk 2077, coinciding with a new update tied to the anime’s story. CDPR stated that âthe anime brings people to the franchise, and the update gives them a reason to play.â The anime boosted the gameâs concurrent player count across all platforms to over 2.1 million players, triple where it was before the anime’s second season premiered.

Roughly half of the studio (513 out of 1051 developers) is now working on The Witcher 4 ahead of a planned 2028 release, with 199 developers working on Cyberpunk 2, a slight increase from earlier this year. This has led to the team working on the studio’s Witcher spin-off, currently titled Sirius, shrinking slightly from 84 developers to a team of 60, while a new IP known as HadarÂ remains in development with a smaller team.

#3618. GTA 6 players are discovering, who needs a gun when it's easier to rob a store with a crate of beer?

Guns might be the weapon of choice for most Grand Theft Auto 6 players, but it turns out some enterprising digital criminals are taking a more inventive approach to robberies. Who needs a gun by their side when you've got a crate of beer?

Ordinarily, when you're attempting a store robbery in GTA 6, you first need to take out the guards - lethally or otherwise - before holding up the staff behind the till. But if you make too much of a commotion, the police show up and things turn sour. So players have been trying all sorts of tricks to avoid raising suspicion. And they've discovered an empty bottle can be thrown at the heads of staff and guards to put them out of action without making a lot of noise. It's non-lethal too!

A post shared by 1- UP Gaming (@1upgaming03)

In a video posted to Instagram, for instance, we see a player casually walking into a jewelry store with a crate of beer under one arm and a swift right hook ready to go in the other. That's when Jason goes on a throwing spree, knocking out staff with some well-placed projectiles to the head and dusting up those who get a little close. Aside from a very brief alarm from a locked door, the robbery goes smoothly.

A post shared by Kotov GTA6 стримы (@kotov.plays)

A faster, less flash example shows a quick and easy shop robbery where a casual bottle to the bloke behind the counter allows for rapid access to the cash in the till. Whether bottles can be utilised for something more complicated, like a full-on bank heist, remains to be seen.

Bottles, though, are just the tip of the iceberg. Roadkill and random lizards on the street also make for handy non-lethal projectiles. Beer remains the more compelling option, however. In gun terms, beer crates have up to six rounds in their 'magazine', making them a reliable single source of stuff to throw at folks.

If you want to try this out yourself, Eurogamer's guide on GTA 6 robberies can get you started. Otherwise, our full GTA 6 walkthrough will take you even further through Rockstar's blockbuster release.

CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss has made headlines for multiple reasons since being hired for the job in October 2025, but one specific aspect of the job she continues to receive backlash for is 60 Minutes. This past summer, Weiss and executive producer Nick Bilton cut ties with several high-profile employees and, more recently, the show has seen losses in viewership. Now, some fresh numbers regarding the news magazine show’s 59th season have arrived, and they mark yet another setback for Weiss and her staff.

Going into this latest season of 60 Minutes, which premiered in September amid the 2026 TV schedule, there was much speculation as to how the show would fare ratings-wise. This latest Nielsen data update from The Wall Street Journal (via The Independent) suggests that the show has indeed been underperforming with its broadcasts. Per the report, the series averaged 8.3 million viewers for the nine episodes that aired between September 9 and November 16. That marks a 16 percent drop from the previous season.

Months ago, Season 59 premiered to 6.5 million viewers on CBS, and that sum differed from the initial report of 7.7 million (which was not finalized at the time). One of the key commonalities between both reports, however, is that the news program has seen losses within the 25-54 demographic. In that demo, 60 has apparently seen a 25 percent decline compared to last season. This demographic is critical, especially when considering on-air advertising.

These ratings mark another less-than-desired situation for CBS News during what’s been a major year of change for 60 Minutes. In May, correspondents Cecilia Vega and Sharyn Alfonsi were fired along with executive producer Tanya Simon and several others. Just recently, Vega said she found it “disturbing” that she still didn’t know the exact reason she was let go. And, shortly after those moves were made, Scott Pelley was also fired from the show after allegedly accusing Weiss of “murdering” the series.

Another topic of discussion revolves around the claims of “journalistic interference” at 60. Series alums like Pelley and Vega have alleged that they were encouraged to insert what they considered to be news bias into their reporting. CBS veteran Dan Rather also chastised Weiss and co. for their reporting. The E-I-C has denied that employees’ editorial autonomy has been taken away from journalists at the company.

With the team at 60 Minutes being aware of the chatter that’s surrounded the show as of late, Bari Weiss recently addressed concerns. She recently spoke at a conference organized by The Information, where she said the show had been doing “tremendously well.” She also emphasized that her main objective for CBS News as a whole was to build a news media organization built on trust. In doing so, she’s made changes to several programs, with the aforementioned show really receiving a makeover.

Bari Weiss Apparently ‘Arrived Like A Conquering Hero’ At CBS News. Why Things Reportedly Changed

After parting ways with Pelley and co., Weiss hired several other broadcasters to fill out 60 Minutes’ new broadcasting team. Ross Douthat, Gianna Toboni, Sebastian Junger, Sir Trevor Phillips and Ariel Levy were ultimately brought on. Those newcomers are now working alongside the show’s three on-camera veterans: Lesley Stahl, Bill Whitaker and Jon Wertheim. Just recently, Stahl addressed the backlash she faced due to remaining with the show under Weiss’ leadership and said she did so in order for the series as they know it not to “vanish.”

There may still be some level of continuity from a talent perspective, but the ratings still stand. As of this writing, neither Bari Weiss nor anyone else from CBS News has addressed this latest viewership update on 60 Minutes. Time will tell how Weiss, Nick Bilton and more might seek to remedy the situation.

#3616. GTA 6 launch knocked Call of Duty's daily players down 42 percent, Alinea estimates

Grand Theft Auto 6's launch took a big bite out of Call of Duty’s player base, according to new estimates from Alinea Analytics, and four days on, it still hasn't recovered.

Writing in Alinea's newsletter, Rhys Elliott said Call of Duty HQ's daily active users (DAUs) across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam fell 42 percent when GTA 6 launched on 19th November, dropping from an average of 7.5 million to 4.4 million. On PlayStation, which Elliott describes as "CoD's main platform", the drop was 44 percent.

"Sadly, CoD has barely bounced back after four days," Elliott wrote. "It's still down 41% from its baseline."

Fortnite and FC 27 took a hit too, but both are already recovering. Fortnite's DAUs on PlayStation and Xbox fell 28 percent, from 17.8 million to 12.8 million, but by the end of the weekend it had clawed its way back to 19 percent below its baseline.

Epic is also holding a live event to close out the current season on 5th December, which Elliott says the studio "hopes will pull players back after they’ve polished off GTA 6’s story".

FC 27's DAUs dropped by around 27 percent, from 5.9 million to 4.3 million, and it's already back within 20 percent of its baseline.

GTA 6's launch hit Call of Duty HARD (@alineaanalytics estimates).COD HQ's daily active users across PlayStation, Xbox, and Steam are down 42% from an average of 7.5M DAUs to 4.4M. On PlayStation – CoD’s main platform – Call of Duty took a 44% hit. Sadly, CoD has barely bounced… pic.twitter.com/XLa6N9TBfr

According to Alinea, of those who'd played GTA 6 by the end of its launch weekend, 29 percent had also played Fortnite this month, 16 percent had played Call of Duty HQ, and 11 percent had played FC 27.

Elliott said the pattern is largely what Alinea had predicted: the big live service games took an instant hit from GTA, but bounced back "because they're ingrained habits". Call of Duty is "the outlier here", he added, "and Xbox should - candidly - be worried about one of its premier franchises".

Elliott also points out that all of this is the impact of GTA 6's single-player mode. He expects its online component and PC port to arrive "some time next year", and when they do, he says, "the bounce back will not be so obtainable".

Alinea also estimates that GTA 6 has sold 44.9 million copies and made more than $4 billion since launch.

GTA 6 launched on Thursday, 19th November, for PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. While it's the biggest entertainment launch of all time, selling 32.5 million pre-release copies and making $3.79 billion by the end of its first day, you wouldn't know it from its Metacritic user score, as players review bomb it over its limited FPS and purported "woke" agenda.

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. If you need help getting through the game now that it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough and a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

According to every Diablo 4 player known to man, I screwed up by skipping its last season. Blizzard shoved just about every iconic Diablo 2 boss and item it could think of into the modern game, and, by all accounts, it was one of the best seasons it ever had.

Even though the Season of Hell's Legacy is about to come to an end, Blizzard has delivered good news for me and everyone else who missed it: Most of it will remain in the game permanently.

On December 1, when the Season of Tyrael's Gambit begins, all of the unique Prime Evil boss fights will still be available, along with the Diablo world boss, Moophisto, and a handful of Diablo 2-inspired items, including the Hellfire Torch Charm. However, the craftable items, like the Enigma chest piece that gives you a free teleport skill, will not carry over.

Even without all the craftable unique items, that's quite a lot of stuff to keep around. Blizzard tends to ditch seasonal additions as soon as a new season starts, and you usually have to wait a while to see them slipped back into the game in a slightly altered form. The overwhelming excitement around the Diablo 2 content must've convinced Blizzard it was worth putting in the work to keep them around.

I would've been happy if the portal to Tristram, the rickety old town at the center of Diablo 2, was all that came back. Blizzard pulled off an incredibly faithful remake of it, complete with the old guitar theme and the voice of the blacksmith Griswold. And if you follow the hidden steps to make the Hellfire Torch, you'll be able to visit Uber Tristram, a special version of the town where you can square off against all three of the series' major villains, the Prime Evils, at once.

Diablo 4 was always kind of light on hidden quests and bosses, so it's nice to see that Blizzard found a way to bring an important part of the series back. I'll be curious to see what else comes to the game over the next three years before Diablo 5 arrives. The Amazon class will drop next year, but no expansions are planned to fill the gap. Hopefully Blizzard will take this opportunity to experiment with more things like the Diablo 2 anniversary secrets before it moves onto the sequel.

#3613. You can expect a similar leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 as there is between GTA 5 and GTA 6, CD Projekt Red says

CD Projekt Red has said people can expect a similar qualitative and technological leap from The Witcher 3 to The Witcher 4 as has been witnessed between Grand Theft Auto 5 and Grand Theft Auto 6.

CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski made the remark during a Q3 earnings call this afternoon, during which he and CDPR faced a handful of questions related to GTA 6.

"First of all, obviously this is a call about us, not about Rockstar," Nowakowski began by saying, "but I do understand the connection here. Having said that, I'm not going to make a deep-dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course we did look at the game, we did see the differences.

"We believe there's going to be a comparable leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 - I think so, yes. It's been 11 years, we are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game, so yes you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Another question was about whether GTA 6 had affected development plans for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 - a question well-timed after Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski joked at the weekend that "Cyberpunk 2 is cancelled" because of how impressive GTA 6 is.

"Is seeing GTA 6 launch making us make the games more expensive?" said Nowakowski. "We have certain ambitions when it comes to Witcher [4] and Cyberpunk 2; they have not changed when it comes to GTA 6. If anything happened as a result of GTA 6, it's [that it's] always great to see games like that because they show you how much cool stuff can be done, and that's for sure an inspiration in many ways for our developers."

Specifically in terms of budget, Nowakowski said nothing had changed, and also echoed a point made earlier this year when he said Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2 are "not budget-driven developments".

"I'm not saying we don't care about the budgets: we do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well. But you cannot make games like that having in mind 'this is the fixed number of money I want to spend and that's it, otherwise I'm gone'," he said.

"They're ambition-driven developments and money's important - the budgets are not indefinite, that's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is like I said, and honestly that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release; it has just always been like that."

When asked whether the arrival of GTA 6 had impacted sales of The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077, Nowakowski answered "yes and no". "You do see a certain dip in engagement on the PlayStation and Xbox for sure," he said.

Statistics apparently show a drop of "at least" 25 percent in CDPR's players as they "engaged themselves with GTA 6". "But you do have to remember that a lot of our players are PC-based," Nowakowski pointed out. "GTA has not launched on PC; we have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales or engagement. So it's a bit of a mixed answer.

"And also on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero," he added. "Some short impact, yes, on the consoles. Long-term, we do not really see that affecting ourselves in any material way in Q4."

Finally, the questioning turned to marketing, which Rockstar has shown can reach far and wide if you have the brand-power of GTA and some imagination. We've seen prestigious department stores like Selfridges taken over by Rockstar for GTA 6, trailers premiering on Netflix, Miami launch festivals - Rockstar's marketing department has gone all out.

CDPR is no stranger to grabbing headlines with glitzy actor hirings such as Keanu Reeves, but will Rockstar's approach to marketing GTA 6 push it a step further?

"The most important takeaway - I'm not sure if I'd call it a lesson because this is our playbook as well - is that if you want to reach a certain critical mass, you do have to get out of just the core gaming bubble, something we did in the past as well," Nowakowski said. "For sure, GTA 6 went there.

"If the underlying question was if we're going to repeat or copy-paste their playbook: no, for sure not. Our games are different and they require a certain different approach - we just do things differently than they do. But in terms of the ultimate effect, in terms of breaking out to the mass market awareness: this is for sure something we consider pivotal to whatever we're going to do with our marketing campaigns in the future."

CDPR's Q3 financial results were positive. The company made less money than this time last year, but the "fresh momentum" - as Nowakowski put it - provided to The Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 by the release of the Remastered edition of Witcher 3 and the Edgerunners anime series on Netflix, and associated game update, went a long way.

The Witcher 3 reached its highest concurrent player count on Steam as a result, and Cyberpunk 2077 reached its second highest concurrent player count, which represents serious staying power for both games so long after they were first released. And with Witcher 3 expansion Songs of the Past on track for 2027, and The Witcher 4 for 2028, the future is loaded.

GTA 6 is the first game in the series to make me feel bad, like really bad, for yeeting innocent cyclists into the Gulf of Leonida with the velocity of a pickup truck at 120 miles per hour. It doesn't stop me from doing it, but every time I find myself covering my mouth with my hand in horror and loading up a previous save, preserving the innocence of a Jason or Lucia without the human-shaped blood splatter on their truck hood. Empathy is another word for the feeling I have toward Leonidans, and it's very much by design.

Rockstar intentionally designed GTA 6 with a built-in criminal profile system that discourages what in-game warnings describe as "psycho" behavior, which is also a permanent label you can acquire if you act like I do consistently without save-scumming. This evolution from Red Dead Redemption 2's honor system is a first for the GTA series and a minor point of contention amid unanimous praise for the game, but Rockstar co-founder Rob Nelson tells Eurogamer that it's simply more fun to play the game as if the NPCs whizzing around the world are actual people. It certainly helps that they look pretty darn close to real humans this time around.

"I think as the resolution goes up, it sort of asks different new questions," says Nelson. "As the resolution goes up, you want the sophistication of the experience to go up, and obviously the sophistication of the mechanics. So it just naturally flowed that we give players choices to interact with the world beyond just violence, beyond just 'down the barrel of a gun', because it's fun ... It's fun for some people like myself to just sort of role-play in the world, and be in the world, and restraint becomes something you hadn't thought about."

Empathy is a bit of a contradiction to the old GTA fantasy of rampaging indiscriminately through a city helpless to your whimsy, but Nelson is right that there's so much more depth to GTA 6 that makes that sort of stuff feel one-dimensional by comparison. Even compared to GTA 5, I find myself exponentially more immersed cruising around Leonidas, and a lot of that comes down to how lifelike its inhabitants are.

"If you think about the NPCs, even back to [GTA] 5, you would draw a weapon - first of all, they didn't react if you drew an invisible shotgun out of nowhere, or a rocket launcher," Nelson says. "They don't react unless you aim it, and then they flee in terror, and you're just sort of this demigod stomping through the world, you know? And that's fun, but for how long?"

If the answer to that question for you is, 'endlessly', you can still choose that life in GTA 6, but you'll eventually reach an irreversible stage in your criminal profile that will permanently alter the way NPCs react and interact with you. "You choose. You're trying to jack somebody off a motorcycle, and they pull a gun on you, and you have to blow their head off and it's like, 'You shouldn't have made me do that!'" Nelson says.

"And so then it has more meaning, and it's more funny in a way when it's a little bit more pointed. And you can still go on those rampages and basically smash your Criminal Profile until it breaks and then you enter this irredeemable state, which basically says 'I reject your criminal profile system! I don't want it.'"

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more

It's a testament to GTA 6's strong writing that I care far too much about Jason and Lucia's relationship to let either of them reach that point in the game's honor system. I'll probably never resist the urge to hijack a nice car in a GTA game, but in this latest iteration, I'll pretty much always load up an old save afterward and role-play as a petty criminal at worst.

It was impossible not to get emotional during The Voice's Dolly Parton tribute night.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

There was no doubt that Dolly Parton tribute night at The Voice would be special. NBC’s long-running singing competition, which is currently airing on the 2026 TV schedule, brought the Top 10 together to perform duets to the greatest hits from the late country icon. It was an hour of performances that were entertaining and emotional as each pairing came from different teams, allowing the coaches to work together in rehearsals for the first time.

All of the performances had an added weight to them because the coaches and singers clearly wanted to do the legendary Dolly Parton justice. After a group performance of “9 to 5” that included an entire troupe of backing dancers, BigCountry (Team Queen) and Dakota Cohen (Team Adam) kicked things off with a rockin’ version of “Jolene” that was big on personality and a fun blend of country and rock. It was smart to start the night with such a jolt of energy, allowing the competitors to keep riding that wave all night.

When it finally came time for the most anticipated song of the night in any Dolly Parton tribute, it was up to Connor Closs (Team Adam) and Brianna Cameron (Team Kelly) to tackle “I Will Always Love You.” A song so big it’s terrifying for any singer to take on, let alone a male vocalist and a 14-year-old, these two beautifully blended their vocals in ways that allowed them to uplift each other and soar even higher. Hands down, it was a showstopper, and it stepped Brianna up as a real contender to win it all.

While it was clear the duet of “I Will Always Love You” stole the show, it definitely wasn’t the only memorable performance of the episode. Ferryn & Brinkley (Team Riley) and Kyle Davis (Team Kelly) were paired up on “Islands in the Stream.” It was already charming that the 61-year-old dad was dueting with sisters who are the age of his own daughters and they had a very father-daughter vibe going on. But the reveal that Ferryn & Brinkley both work full-time at Dollywood, the amusement park owned by Dolly Parton herself, and that they even had footage of Ferryn on stage with the icon was really special to see.

Since first appearing at the Blind Auditions, Ferryn & Brinkley have been hugely marketable. From their talent to their personalities, they look and feel like they could easily join the ranks of country stars who've also broken big in movies and TV, whether they ultimately win The Voice or not. As we move ever closer to the unveiling of the winning coach and star, it’s getting harder and harder to watch the singers get sent home, but I get the feeling that many of them are going to have a life in entertainment beyond this season.

The only real complaint I’ve had about the Live Shows has been the lack of coach banter and shenanigans, which was absolutely delightful earlier in the season. Seeing Dolly Parton in past The Voice appearances being her sassy self really helped make up for some of that and was a fitting way to remember her.

The Voice Season 30 will continue to air on NBC on Mondays until the two-hour finale on December 14th when the winner is finally crowned. You can also watch the next day with a Peacock subscription.

#3610. The Steam Awards turn 10 with throwback categories and a Game of the Year Hall of Fame

Nominations for the 2026 Steam Awards are now open, and to mark the event's 10th anniversary, Valve has brought back some categories from years past and added a Hall of Fame.

You've got until 6pm UK (10am Pacific) on 30th November to nominate your favourite games of the year across 14 categories. Returning throwbacks include Just 5 More Minutes, Defies Description, and This is My Job Now, which recognises games that simulate mundane real-life jobs.

The new Hall of Fame category will appear when voting opens, and will let players choose their favourite from Steam's previous Game of the Year winners to crown the best game of the past decade.

Most categories are only open to games released on Steam since last year's Autumn Sale.

The exception is the Labo(u)r of Love award, which goes to older games that developers are still supporting with new content. Previous Labo(u)r of Love winners, including Warframe, Grand Theft Auto 5, Cyberpunk 2077, and Baldur's Gate 3, can't be nominated again.

Five finalists will be revealed in each category when voting opens alongside the Steam Winter Sale on 17th December. Voting closes at 10am Pacific on 2nd January, and the winners will be announced straight afterwards.

Nominating in at least one category also earns you the first level of Steam's Nomination Committee badge.

Earlier this month, Valve released a new Steam update that adds Steam Deck framerate data to a game's store page, giving potential buyers an indication of how well a game runs on the handheld.

#3609. Wait, What? GTA 6 Runs Better On Xbox Series X Than PS5

Digital FoundryGrand Theft Auto VIGTA 6Rockstar

When it comes toÂ GTA 6, PlayStation has very much been the teacher’s pet. Microsoft was operating under a weird-ass ban that prevented it from marketing the fact that the game was coming out on its console, while the PS5 has been broadly promoted as the natural home for Rockstar’s record-breaking release. And yet, Digital Foundry‘s latest analysis ofÂ GTA 6‘s performance across all four of Microsoft and Sony’s current-gen systems shows the Series X outdoing the PS5. “Ultimately,” the site’s boffins report, “Series X is meaningfully better off.”

It’s important to mention right away that the PS5 Pro still wipes the floor with the Series X, and is without doubt the best way to play Grand Theft Auto VI until the official PC version is released. But when you measure the two base machines between the rival console makers,Â DF says there’s no doubt that it’s the Series X that edges ahead of the PS5.

Both consoles offer “a virtually identical visual presentation,” say the tech experts, with nothing to divide them in all the important areas. But when it comes to performance, this is where Xbox takes the lead. Both machines struggle during “heavy vehicle traversal” and “intense airport crowd sequences,” but the PS5 “suffers substantially more frequent frame-rate drops” than the Series X, “which is compounded by the fact that the Xbox machine also benefits from 120Hz VRR support to smooth out minor dips.”

Unsurprisingly, the Series S performs the poorest out of all four, but actually offers better results than anyone was expecting. While its framerate drops are horrible, frequently dipping into the teens, the use of PSR 4.1 upscaling and a reduction in the most intensive details still has it looking pretty lovely. It’s definitely not a great way to play the game, but it’s less terrible than you’d think.

So there you go, Xbox owners: you’re not the ugly stepsister you might have been made to feel like. Obviously the differences remain slight, and with both consoles (and even the PS5 Pro) capped to 30 FPS there are compromises to be made by all, so whether you’re playing on PlayStation or Xbox Series X, you’re mostly having the same experience. But Xbox owners have earned themselves a quietly smug grin.

GTA 6 could be a PC game (illegally) in a matter of days.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Update 11/25/26: Projects are reporting progress in loading shaders on AMD hardware, but framerates remain in the single digits. We've updated the "top five" projects according to Portwatch VI.

Things are moving fast. Now that an illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 is out in the wild, anonymous modders are racing to port it to PC, and the work is progressing faster than many expected. At this rate, it's possible that a static recompilation of GTA 6 will run on a PC in a matter of days. It's also possible it will take much longer to produce a playable build that's actually on par with the console versions.

What we do know for sure is that Rockstar is taking notice and has already begun cracking down on the highest-profile projects. As always, downloading pirated software is illegal and can infect your PC with malware, and that last bit is doubly true in the dubious AI era we now live in.

For now, the only thing to do is observe and report. Here's where things stand with GTA 6 PC ports.

Several projects have made it as far as booting the game and using menus, and at least one has seemingly managed to move around in-game with bugged out lighting, but it's hard to verify clips making the rounds when so many are obvious fakes.

Dozens of groups of anonymous modders and vibecoders. So many, in fact, that several websites dedicated to tracking the progress of GTA 6 recomp efforts have also appeared. One of the tracker sites, Portwatch VI, has a list of projects ranked by their "playable" completion percentage—best not to take those made up figures as an accurate estimate of when a port will be complete. The top five are:

Until very recently, the Leonida project was among those making impressive progress, but the group's creator (a 15-year-old) quit the project after Rockstar got its Discord server taken down.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

Every GTA 6 recomp project is based on the same thing: An illicit Xbox build of GTA 6 released online by Cyberleek, the notorious leaker who previously shared video of a GTA 6 development build months before its release.

With GTA 6 being the biggest game in the world at the moment and not available on PC, there is an outsized motivation to get it running.

A recomp refers to static recompilation, which is the result of reverse-engineering a game's code to make it run on other hardware (usually a PC). If you want to read further on how that's achieved, PCG alum Wes Fenlon's excellent Read Only Memo newsletter has what you're looking for.

As for how GTA 6 ports (and ports for other new games) are coming together so quickly, the answer is AI. The advent of AI coding tools like Claude have greatly expedited the work required to create a static recompilation of games on another platform. What used to take months to years now takes hours to days. Recomps that heavily use AI are often buggier, messier, and have fewer features than human-made fan projects, but they are fast and functional.

It's way too early to speak in absolutes, but I'm comfortable assuming that the first "playable" recomps will require an exceptionally powerful PC.

That guess is based on GTA 6 being an obviously demanding game and also some recent precedent: The earliest Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake recomps that've appeared online have high system requirements to perform as well as it does natively on Switch 2—and, well, GTA 6 has a lot more happening under the hood than a 28-year-old Zelda game.

That's the big question. My money is on no, it won't. To switch up plans on a dime would assume that Rockstar is sitting on a polished PC version that it could put out any day, and I'm not convinced that's the case. The current rumor, preceding all of this leak business, is that the PC version of GTA 6 is planned for Q1 2027 (so anytime before April).

That's not to say Rockstar couldn't expedite the process if it wanted to—they certainly have the resources to achieve the unlikely.

#3607. Lords of the Fallen 2 delayed to April 2027, exact release date coming next month

Lords of the Fallen 2 will now launch in April 2027, and we'll find out exactly when next month.

The news came via a short post on X from CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski. "Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027," he wrote. "Exact date in December."

That means the Soulslike sequel has slipped again. Back in June, CI Games pushed Lords of the Fallen 2 into a Q1 2027 release window, saying the extra time would let the team refine the game and keep it clear of "a highly competitive holiday period". That was a delay in itself, as when CI Games and Epic ended the game's PC exclusivity deal in May, it was still targeting a 2026 release.

Last month, CI Games secured a €28.6 million (around $32 million) loan to complete production and release Lords of the Fallen 2, as well as refinance its existing bank debt, according to a stock exchange filing. The loan matures on 31st August 2027, and, as reported at the time, CI Games will self-publish the game and expects to repay the loan through its sales.

Lords of the Fallen II: April 2027. Exact date in December. pic.twitter.com/yYaevDqaxe

Lords of the Fallen 2 is coming to PS5, Xbox Series X/S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store.

Following its announcement in 2025 and a look at gameplay during that year's The Game Awards, Lords of the Fallen 2 - which is technically the series' third game if we don't ignore the fact it was rebooted - had been steadily marching towards an unspecified 2026 launch. On PC, the plan was for it to be an Epic Games Store exclusive, but that's no longer happening after we learned CI Games - developer and sole owner of the IP - is now free from the multi-year exclusivity deal with Epic Games.

The sequel has also been at the centre of heated conversations following CI Games founder and CEO Marek Tyminski's comments regarding "political correctness" and "real player feedback". The studio also raised eyebrows recently by announcing more revealing armour sets for female characters in Lords of the Fallen 2, for instance, compared to its previous project.

Eurogamer gave the rebooted Lords of the Fallen two stars, calling it "a perfectly acceptable Soulslike that's often fun to play and offers the same satisfaction at overcoming adversity", but one let down by "Soulslike clichés and performance woes".

#3606. The Normal Person’s Guide To Understanding Grand Theft Auto 6

Grand Theft Auto 6 is everywhere you look. Every news channel is talking about it. Celebrities and musicians are playing GTA 6 or posting about its release. It’s apparently the biggest game ever and has sold nearly 40 million copies already. But if you aren’t a big gamer or not a video game fan at all, you might have questions. I have answers.

Perhaps someone sent you this link because you kept asking them GTA 6 questions. Maybe you did a Google search, made it past the AI results and found this blog explaining what GTA 6 is to people who don’t buy or play games. Whatever the case, welcome. I’m going to walk you through what is almost certainly the biggest video game launch of the decade, why people are going so wild, and what the game actually is and isn’t.

It is an open-world game that mixes together a lot of video game genres, like driving, shooting, and exploration. As with most open-world games, you can run around freely or do story missions. It’s up to the player. You control two characters, Jason and Lucia, who are criminals on the run in fictional versions of Florida and Miami named Leonida and Vice City, respectively.

More or less, yeah. The developer, Rockstar Games, has been working on this game since at least 2015 or so. Turns out creating a photorealistic recreation of a chunk of Florida that players can explore and do whatever they want in takes time!

No. You can buy it on either PS5 or Xbox for $80. The $100 version comes with a bunch of extra outfits, hairstyles, and other items players can wear or buy in-game using cash they collect from crimes, but it’s definitely not required.

It took me about 90 hours to reach the end of the main story. I’ve since played over 150 hours, and I’m still finding new stuff, hearing new songs, and seeing new random events. Yeah, it’s big.

Well, a lot of people have been waiting for 13 years to play GTA 6. The last new GTA game, GTA V, was released back in 2013. So anticipation for this game has been building for a long time. And, surprisingly, GTA 6 lived up to the hype.

There are a few reasons for the glowing critical reception. The game’s narrative is really good, featuring two extremely well-written characters that develop a meaningful relationship over the course of its five chapters. Another big reason for the high review scores is just how expansive and reactive the world is. Characters in the game will comment on your clothes, respond to your actions, and remember things you did hours and hours ago. It’s also a lot of fun to play, with challenging but rewarding driving, combat, and police encounters. And it looks incredible, with some of the best graphics ever seen in a console game. Some critics are calling it the best game of the year. And many players are calling it one of the best games ever.

GTA: Vice City on the PS2 was much, much smaller and less advanced (though in some ways it was pretty advanced for the time) and was set in the 1980s. While Vice City is a major location in GTA 6, this is an unconnected and different version of the city from that seen in the original 2002 PS2 game.

So many things! Players can steal cars, drive boats, get into fist fights, shoot at the cops, go fishing, play mini-golf, hit the gun range, pet dogs, scuba dive, fly planes, explore the swamps, hunt deer, join in street races, visit the beach, get drunk, buy clothes, play fake video games inside the game, take a shower, eat food, work out, blow up cars, or just chill in a bar. You can also just play through the game’s main story, which is all about Jason and Lucia trying to make some money as criminals to build a life for themselves and their son.

Yes, Jason and Lucia have a child, a fact which was omitted from any pre-release marketing but is revealed in the first 20 minutes of the game. During the events of the game, he is living with his aunt while Lucia and Jason do whatever they can to make a good life for him and get him back.

She is an attractive but disturbing character players meet very early in the game who may or may not be a serial killer or creepy stalker. Despite this, many people online still want to have sex with her. Some players also think Jason should hook up with Mandy and ditch Lucia. These people are wrong.

No. While you can do that stuff, GTA 6 doesn’t force you to be a good boyfriend. You can be a real jerk to Lucia, and she can be a real asshole to Jason. Also, the chores players are talking about only make up a few minutes of the opening hours of GTA 6. The rest of the game has none of that stuff in it.

Like the chores mentioned already, these elements are optional. If you constantly skip working out, your characters will eventually become less ripped and might even develop small bellies and thicker thighs. But you can still play all the missions and shoot cops.

What? You can totally shoot random people, cops, and more.

That’s not accurate. You can shoot, punch, tackle, burn, run over, drown, choke, and slap women.

Uhh, you can steal cars. Some cars, like very fancy cars, have special security measures, so you can’t steal them as easily, but you can walk up to any person driving a car at a stoplight, rip them out and take their ride.

Okay, so, something you need to understand about GTA 6 is that it is at the center of a massive online culture war. Conservative players, grifters, chuds, and other weirdos are currently spreading false information about this game online. There are also plenty of people online posting inflammatory nonsense to get clicks and engagement on sites like Twitter that reward that shit. So if you read something kind of wild about this game, just know it might be false. Check places like Kotaku or other major gaming sites to verify.

Well, actually, Rockstar did remove sex workers you can pay to have sex with from GTA 6. But there are still strippers in the game.

Yes, GTA V has GTA Online, a very popular, successful, and still-ongoing multiplayer game with millions of players. This time around, it seems Rockstar wanted to focus all its resources on getting GTA 6 out the door without also having to finish a big online mode. That said, I find it very hard to believe that GTA 6 won’t get some kind of multiplayer mode in the future.

Never. I mean, officially, Rockstar hasn’t said that, but based on how the game looks and how it runs on the Series S, the weakest console it is currently available on, I’m very doubtful a Switch 2 port is coming anytime soon.

There is a lot of nudity in this game. You can shoot people’s heads off. You can burn them alive. A big part of the game involves robbing stores and selling drugs. I say all that not to suggest your kid or teenager shouldn’t play the game, but just to let you know what’s waiting for them in Vice City. Ultimately, it’s up to you and what you think your kid can handle. Either way, just know they are already totally seeing clips of this game online on places like TikTok.

This year, we’ve talked a lot about Taylor Swift’s wedding and her song in Toy Story 5. However, amid chatter about her CMA performance and her supporting Travis Kelce at his games, the conversation about the pop star has shifted to a Vanity Fair story about her image and rise to fame. Many have called it a “hit piece” about the singer (who is never explicitly named in it). So, now, as people continue to discuss the claims made, one of the pop star’s former classmates, who is quoted in the piece, is clearing the air about her Ugg boot comments.

In a piece published by Vanity Fair, it goes over a comment Swift made early in her career about not having friends when she was younger. That is followed by claims from a classmate, Chanice Skinner, about how she was “always part of the popular crowd.” She also claimed that Swift was “one of the bullies.” After that, she said she thinks Swift’s parents funded her dream.

Then came the part about the Ugg boots. Arielle Peppers, who also went to school with the pop star, shared that tale, and it was told in the VF piece as follows:

Arielle Peppers was a year behind The Star and sat on the other side of Skinner in Luyben’s class for multiple quarters. She remembers The Star coming to class in Ugg boots. Peppers had transferred from the nearby city of ReAding after her neighbor was stabbed in the neck. She asked her mother for a pair of the same boots. ‘Do you know how much they cost?’ her mother said. A pair of Uggs amounted to half her single mother’s paycheck working variously at a bakery, at a dairy mill, and as a caretaker. Peppers recalls The Star owning multiples of Uggs: ‘She had the brown one, the black one, the blue one.’

Along with this story about the Uggs, Peppers explained that she saw Swift get teased at a school talent show after she sang a song about a crush.

In the wake of this story going live, the comments about the Uggs have gone viral. One tweet in particular said their “favorite part” of the piece was when it covered someone “harboring a legitimate grudge over Taylor owning Uggs.” Many others commented on this quote, too. However, Peppers wants to clear the air.

Arielle Peppers wants to make it clear she was not trying to throw shade at Taylor Swift. During an interview with TMZ, she explained that, too, saying:

I shared a straightforward childhood memory with a reporter about school and what was affordable for different families at the time. It wasn't intended as an attack on anyone.

This former classmate was one of the very few sources named in the Vanity Fair piece. While May Jeong interviewed more than 100 sources, many stayed anonymous. In the wake of the story being published, Peppers said she’s gotten threats and had to deal with online chaos and hate. Overall, she just wants to focus on her own life, as she told TMZ:

I'm focused on my own life, raising my twin daughters, working, and pursuing my own musical goals as A. Star. I wish Taylor Swift continued success.

She ended by saying she wants to “move forward with positivity and love.” Meanwhile, a source alleged to Page Six that Swift, who is no stranger to online hate and speculation, “isn’t going to lose sleep over any of this.”

Between her ongoing Oscar campaign for her Toy Story 5 song, the anticipation and theories surrounding the potential re-release of her first album and more, she’s clearly got a lot going on at the moment. And when it comes to the Uggs, her former classmate made it clear that she meant no harm by these comments that went viral.

#3603. Performance analysis reveals GTA 6 has a more stable frame-rate on Xbox Series X compared to PlayStation 5

If you don't own a PlayStation 5 Pro, the best way to play Grand Theft Auto 6 is reportedly on Xbox Series X. That's according to new performance analysis, which shows Microsoft's console is more consistent at maintaining the game's 30fps frame-rate target than the base PS5.

The findings come from the tech experts Digital Foundry, who published a big report covering all the technical similarities and differences between Sony and Microsoft's consoles.

Unsurprisingly, PS5 Pro is in the lead with no competition, as Xbox elected not to release a mid-generation upgrade for the Series console family. Sony's more powerful console delivers "the definitive console GTA 6 experience," according to Digital Foundry. The PS5 Pro has the most stable 30fps performance of all four consoles, and benefits from a sharper presentation at 4K thanks to Sony's PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) image upscaler, which upscales the image from a 1440p base resolution.

It's when comparing the base consoles - Xbox Series X and PS5 - that things get a little more interesting. Both target a 30fps frame-rate and often maintain that target, but certain sections trigger drops. According to the report, those include sequences with busy crowds and fast vehicle traversal. In some cases, the drops can be as low as mid-to-high 20fps.

With that in mind, PS5 has "substantially more frequent" frame-rate drops compared to Series X. The Xbox console is also aided by its support for 120Hz Variable Refresh Rate (VRR), which helps smooth out small dips in the frame-rate.

"Ultimately, Series X is meaningfully better off," Digital Foundry concluded.

Despite the studio's close marketing alignment with PlayStation historically - to the point Xbox can't even say GTA 6 in certain posts about GTA 6 - this is not the first time a Rockstar game has run better or looked better on an Xbox console.

At Red Dead Redemption 2's launch in 2018, Digital Foundry hailed Xbox One X as the best place to play it, owing to - unsurprisingly - a more stable 30fps frame-rate and sharper visuals. Not much has changed in the past eight years on that front, then.

Given all the information we have today, including the lack of 60fps and 40fps modes on PS5 Pro, it's going to be really interesting to see the kind of PC specs required to achieve parity with console visuals at 60fps and beyond. If Rockstar doesn't get there first, modders are already working on porting GTA 6 to PC.

Nvidia's latest GeForce Game Ready driver, version 621.40, is out now. "This new Game Ready Driver provides the best gaming experience for Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War 4, and Assetto Corsa Rally," the notes say, "and the addition of DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering to Where Winds Meet."

Which is kind of burying the lead. This patch is really a hotfix for a hotfix, an update that finally addresses the bug with previous driver packages that had them pointlessly rewriting a log file over and over, quickly adding up to tens of GB every hour and potentially damaging SSDs nobody can afford to replace any more.

Over the weekend Nvidia released a hotfix that supposedly caught the bug, only for users to discover it merely delayed its onset. Rather than setting in immediately after a reboot, it would wait until your PC had been on for a while before shitting the bed. If you're one of the people who leaves your computer running overnight then I hope you stayed on version 621.01, the last safe driver package before the current one.

Forum users have been testing out version 621.40 and it seems to have not only stopped the Nvidia container service from freaking out and rewriting its log, but also caught a bug with custom cursors that would make them turn gray. Which is nice.

I'm tempted to play it safe and stay on my old driver anyway, though I'll update for Dawn of War 4, which comes out on December 3. #3599. Capcom's sci-fi dinosaur shooter Exoprimal is shutting down next year

Sad news dinosaur lovers. Exoprimal - Capcom's third-person sci-fi shooter with a Jurassic twist - will be shutting down next year. With its closure, the game will no longer be playable, even for those who've got it downloaded.

In a new post to the official Exoprimal website, it's revealed the game will be shuttered on 29th September 2027, at 8am PDT across all regions. Until then, all Survival Passes (battle pass equivalents) are no longer available for purchase, with the game and all its DLC stripped from stores on 30th March.

If you do fancy hopping in for a bit to send off Exoprimal in style, you'll still be able to re-download the game after it's taken off stores if you originally downloaded the game in the past. Tragically, the game will no longer be playable at all once shuttered, as there's no offline support. As an always-online game that requires a constant internet connection, it'll be one for the history books, at least in an official capacity.

Exoprimal was an interesting game for certain. A spin on the popular hero shooter, the game blended staples from the genre with some fairly cool twists. For one, the PvE elements were immediately interesting: seeing waves of raptors race towards you and your allies was critical to its appeal. On top of that, the PvPvE elements where two teams would race to complete objectives was pretty neat, thanks in large part to a variety of enjoyable exosuits at your disposal.

Even so, the game never really caught on to the extent that its peers did. Many pointed to the premium price tag paired with in-game microtransactions as a core factor to this, believing it would be hard to convince someone to play the game over something like Overwatch, which was free. Still, it had nearly a million players soon after launch, with Capcom stating it expected the game to be profitable in a financial report following the game's release. Whether or not it actually was remains unclear.

With that in mind, pay some mind to the Exoprimal players who don't have too long left with their game of choice. All the Krieger players out there have my sympathies. All the Vigilant players do not.

CD Projekt Red reported its Q3 earnings today, but all anyone wanted to talk about was GTA 6.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

CD Projekt made its Q3 2026 financial report today, and there's not a whole lot to see: The Witcher 3 remaster was a big hit, work on Cyberpunk 2 and The Witcher 4 is ticking along, and everyone really liked Cyberpunk: Edgerunners 2.

Perhaps understandably, a number of questions in the subsequent investors call put the focus on Grand Theft Auto 6. While CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski didn't go too deep on the topic, he did say that the upcoming Witcher 4 will be comparable to GTA 6 in at least one way.

"Obviously, this is a call about us, not about Rockstar, but I do understand the connection here," Nowakowski said when asked if The Witcher 4 will represent a technological leap over its predecessor comparable to GTA 6. "Having said that, of course, I'm not going to make a deep dive and a full-blown review of GTA 5 versus GTA 6. But of course, we did look at the game. We did see the differences.

"Do we believe there's going to be a comparable leap between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4? I think so, yes. I mean, it's been 11 years. We are working on The Witcher 4 to make it significantly better looking and improved in terms of pretty much every possible facet of the game. So yes, you should expect us to make a much bigger jump between Witcher 3 and Witcher 4."

Well, sure. As Nowakowski said, The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt was released 11 years ago, and it'll be two more years before The Witcher 4 comes out—assuming it's not delayed, which would make it a rarity among CD Projekt games. It will also be the same number of years between Witcher 3 and 4 as spanned GTA 5 and 6. In the world of technology, 13 years is a long time.

Hell, just the upgrade from the original Witcher 3 to the remastered version that dropped earlier this year is notable:

At the same time, Nowakowski said that while the GTA 6 launch was tremendously successful, CD Projekt Red doesn't intend to merely mimic Rockstar's approach when The Witcher 4 is ready to go: "Our games are different and the require a certain different approach, and we just do certain things differently than they do."

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

He also said that while the release of GTA 6 has had an impact on Witcher 3 and Cyberpunk 2077 sales on consoles, he doesn't expect it to have a "material impact" on the company's Q4 finances for one obvious reason.

"You do have to remember that a lot of our players are also PC-based," Nowakowski said. "GTA has not launched on PC. We have not seen any impact whatsoever on the PC sales on engagement." And, he added, "on the PS5 and Xbox, it's not like our sales came to zero."

Nowakowsi also said that GTA 6 hasn't changed CD Projekt's ambitions for The Witcher 4 and Cyberpunk 2: If anything, it's "an inspiration in many ways for our developers." And he's not concerned about its success pushing up development budgets, because CD Projekt's games "are not budget-driven developments."

"I'm not saying that we don't care about the budgets. We do, and I'm pretty sure [Rockstar] did as well," Nowakowski said. "But you cannot make games like that having in mind, 'This is the fixed number of money I want to spend, and that's it. Otherwise, we're gone.'

"They are ambition-driven developments and money is important. The budgets are not indefinite. That's not what we're saying. But the philosophy is kind of like I said. And honestly, that philosophy has not changed for us because of GTA 6's release. It has just always been like that."

Nowakowski's positive take on GTA 6 isn't too far off that of Cyberpunk 2 creative director Igor Sarzynski, who said yesterday that he's suffering from "GTA 6-induced-open-world-game-dev-depression," although he quickly clarified that CD Projekt is "doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor." (And that he wasn't being serious about cancelling Cyberpunk 2.)

seriously though i think we're doing something of our own, with a different unique flavor. GTA is impressive in a way all great art is, it expands what is possible, a captivating vision flawlessly executed

The Witcher 4 is currently slated for launch sometime in 2028, while Cyberpunk 2 isn't expected out before 2030.

#3596. Pikachu And Mario Might Not Fly As Gale Force Winds Threaten The 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade (Update: It’s Been Delayed!)

Macy's Thanksgiving Dad ParadeMarioPikachuThanksgiving

Tomorrow morning, millions of people are planning to tune in to watch the famous annual Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City, with its iconic giant balloons. However, balloons like Mario and Pikachu might remain grounded due to forecasts predicting extremely nasty weather.

Update: 4:00 PM EST – As reported by NBC, the parade has officially been delayed until Saturday. This is the first time in the 100-year history of the parade that it has been delayed. Mario’s mustache will fly… later.

Meteorologists are forecasting a truly nasty Thanksgiving morning in NYC, with a high-wind warning currently set to kick off at 10 a.m. Eastern Time. Gusts are projected to possibly reach as high as 60 mph and sustained winds could clock in at around 35 mph, reported Hell Gate. Weather experts are also predicting power outages and fallen tree limbs across the city.

This is the kind of weather that could force parade officials to keep balloons lower to the ground or even prevent them from flying at all due to safety concerns and legal restrictions that were placed on the parade after the infamous 1997 parade that saw multiple balloons, including Sonic the Hedgehog, damaged by winds and multiple injuries reported. During that disaster, wind gusts reached around 43 mph, well below what’s forecasted for tomorrow.

As reported by ABC 7, parade officials won’t make a decision until early Thursday morning, before the start of the parade. One option is to fly balloons much lower to the ground. Another option being floated by officials is to start the parade earlier than 8:30 am to hopefully avoid the worst of the incoming storm.

“This is a challenging week. This is a challenging forecast,” New York City Emergency Management Commissioner Christina Farrell told ABC7.

“You may remember, there was some lightning and storms coming through on July 4th. It’s been that kind of year. The fireworks were moved up a little bit. That is one option. If the weather is coming in a little later, can we start things a little earlier?” said Farrell.

Video gameâthemed balloons are planned to be part of the parade, including a Mario balloon celebrating the home release of The Super Mario Galaxy Movie and a Pikachu and Eevee balloon first seen in 2021.Â  Last year, Mario opened the event. Pac-Man is also reportedly set to fly tomorrow in the parade, assuming the balloons aren’t grounded.

This is the 100th year of the iconic NYC parade, a major milestone. Across its 100-year history, it has never been canceled. And while the Macy’s Parade has happened in rainy, stormy weather before, tomorrow might prove too much, leaving Mario, Pikachu, and Eevee stuck on West 77th Street.

Last year during the parade, NBC reporter Savannah Guthrie claimed that “no one has a better mustache” than Mario. Hopefully, we all get to see it fly Thursday morning.

#3595. Kristen Bell, Andie MacDowell, Eva Longoria, and More Honor Community Builders at L’Oréal Paris’s Women of Worth Gala

L’Oréal Paris welcomed its latest Women of Worth honorees with an intimate, elegant gala in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. For the annual celebration, which honors unsung nonprofit leaders, guests gathered at The Ebell of Los Angeles, a venue with a rich history of its own.

The evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

As the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director said, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”

L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she said. She then welcomed the company’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone showed up and showed out,” she said, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance company with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

During a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she said. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

#3594. CD Projekt Red signs new marketing partnership deal with Sony for The Witcher 4, and to increase "the presence" of its games on PlayStation

As part of The Witcher and Cyberpunk studio CD Projekt Red's recent Q3 earnings report, the developer offered some updates on upcoming game The Witcher 4.

During an earnings call yesterday, the studio revealed it had signed a new partnership deal with Sony regarding marketing rights to The Witcher 4, as well as to extend "the presence" of CD Projekt Red's other games across the PlayStation Store and PlayStation Plus.

"Just today, we signed new partnership agreements with Sony Interactive Entertainment covering the presence of our games on PlayStation and in PlayStation Plus subscriptions, as well as our collaboration during the upcoming Witcher 4 marketing campaign," said studio CFO Piotr Nielubowicz. "This cooperation will support our business and financial outlook in this and future years."

Nielubowicz didn't elaborate on what exactly that means for The Witcher 4's marketing, but perhaps it could enable Sony to advertise the action-RPG as a PlayStation game, similar to the Grand Theft Auto 6 'plays best on PlayStation' campaign. But seeing as The Witcher 4 is currently targeting a 2028 release, we may not find out what form that agreement takes for some time.

That said, looking at similar marketing agreements from Sony's recent history, we can probably expect The Witcher 4 to show up during Sony State of Play presentations or even have dedicated PlayStation-focused showcases. The Witcher 4 footage may also be specified as being captured on PlayStation hardware - something we already saw with The Witcher 4 tech demo last year. Perhaps we'll see Witcher-themed accessories and PlayStation hardware, too.

This is a notable shift for CDPR, which has historically had close ties to Xbox. Cyberpunk 2077's big Keanu Reeves reveal (as Johnny Silverhand) took place on Xbox's E3 2019 stage, and The Witcher 3's reveal happened on Microsoft's E3 2013 stage. Going further back, Xbox 360 was the only console The Witcher 2 was released on.

During the same earnings call, CDPR joint-CEO Michał Nowakowski said that we should expect the leap between The Witcher 3 and The Witcher 4 to be similar to that between GTA 5 and GTA 6, while also praising Rockstar's approach to marketing its record-breaking new game.

The Hunger Games star should obviously play a Gold... but which one?

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Now that we know that a Red Rising movie is in the works, it's completely understandable that we'd be on the edges of our seats waiting for any word on who might be cast in the book-to-screen adaptation. Eagle-eyed Red Rising fans -- yes, that's an intentional nod to the Bellona sigil right there -- have picked up on the fact that author Pierce Brown has followed Joseph Zada on Instagram, which has led to a lot of enthusiastic speculation that the Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping star might be in talks to play a role in Red Rising movie. I've seen one specific character name coming up a lot as the perfect role for Zada to take on, but wait a second, because there are options here.

To be clear up front, there is no official word that Zada is in talks to star in the Red Rising movie. However, it's not a stretch that his name would be circulating. As mentioned, fans noticed Pierce Brown followed Zada on Instagram. Then there's the fact that Zada is currently starring in Francis Lawrence's most recent movie adaptation. Given the news that Lawrence will be directing the Red Rising movie, it stands to reason that he might be considering people he's worked with already for the cast.

On the other hand, the fact that Pierce Brown and Francis Lawrence have known each other for years (per Lawrence) also needs to be acknowledged, as Brown could've met Zada through the director and followed him just to follow him... as people do. In short, the follow could mean nothing or it could mean something.

However, since we're speculating, I want to talk about the role(s) he'd be right to take, starting with the one that seems to be a crowd favorite.

The handsome Bellona's name came up quite a bit in the comments discussing who Zada should play, and I get it. Even as Golds go, Cassius is known to be extremely handsome, and well, Zada fits that description. Zada's also got the blond curls, which is one of the most distinctive things about Cassius' looks. Also, as a Gold, Cassius is tall, and so is Zada.

When it comes to casting the Gold characters (and Obsidians) in the movie, it seems unlikely that they're going to find the perfect actors to play the roles, who also just so happen to be around or above seven feet tall. How they make the size differences among the colors stand out on screen is going to be a challenge by itself, whether they use forced perspective, special effects or other techniques. Still, if they want to cast actors on the taller side for the Golds, IMDB has Zada listed as 6'2".

Relative to men of average height, Zada's reported height (or anywhere in the ballpark of six feet, really) seems like a good fit for a Gold on screen. That brings me to the alternate speculation, because I don't think Cassius is the only option, or possibly even the best one.

Darrow's the other name I've seen circulating, and honestly, he's the first person I thought of when I saw the topic of Joseph Zada possibly starring in the Red Rising movie. Maybe it's seeing him play a District 12 kid in Sunrise on the Reaping that makes it easier for me to envision him as a lowRed with a score to settle. There are a lot of sides to Darrow, especially when we factor in the teen that he is at the start of Red Rising, and the transition (and drama) he goes through in the first book. I can see Zada tackling that arc really well.

Nah. I can't even picture it... but it'd be fun to see his take on the role.

I'm going to cross Pax off the list right away. Even if Zada bulked up a lot for the part, I picture a guy with the size and personality of a jovial (or ferocious, when necessary) bear for the youngest Telemanus son. However, Roque would be an interesting option. I don't think Zada fits how I imagine Roque to look, but I do think he'd have an interesting take on the thoughtful character.

The last person I considered was The Jackal. While his role in the first book is fairly limited -- he's present more by reputation than he actually is on page -- he does get one of the most memorable scenes, and after playing the hero in the Hunger Games movie, I really wouldn't mind seeing what Zada does with a dark and twisty character like The Jackal.

Whether or not Zada gets cast in the Red Rising movie remains to be seen, but he does seem like a great candidate for a role, and from what he told Xtra, it sounds like he's interested in being involved.
